title: ZPA Appliance Wall and Rack Mount Instruction Manual

blocks.text: This article includes instructions on mounting your ZPA appliance.

Mounting your ZPA appliance on a rack or wall optimizes your workspace and makes the appliance more accessible for installation and deployment. It also protects the appliance from any external damage and helps streamline the organization of cables and power adapters. Additionally, rack or wall mounting helps ensure proper airflow, preventing overheating and dust accumulation caused by restricted ventilation. Proper airflow also maintains a cleaner environment, prolonging the lifespan of the appliance.
The ZPA appliance ships in the following form factors: hosting either the App Connector or the Private Service Edge for Private Access (ZPA).

blocks.item: The ZS-ZPA-APPL-800-APPC appliances are rack-mountable form factors. You can also use the wall mount kit, available by request. These instructions are structured to assist IT personnel with the physical mounting, cabling, and initial power on of the appliance. This guide solely focuses on the hardware installation process and doesn’t cover software configuration. For software configuration, see Deploying App Connector and Private Service Edge ZPA Appliances.

blocks.item: Before beginning the installation, verify that all necessary components are present in the packaging. The package includes the following items:
6x A screws for attaching the brackets to the appliance
The wall mount kit is available only by request.
Turn the appliance over and attach the wall brackets onto the bottom side of the appliance. Secure with the 4x B screws provided for mounting.
On the wall, measure the exact place where you want to mount the appliance. Drill 4 holes that align with the 4 mounting holes on the brackets.
Insert the 4 white wall plugs into the holes you drilled into the wall.
Insert the long screws into the wall plugs.
Align the 4 screw holes on the appliance's wall brackets with the 4 long screws installed on the wall.
Secure the 4 screws in the bracket holes, and push the appliance downward to lock the screws into position.
Connect the necessary cables to the designated ports of the appliance. To learn more, see ZPA Appliance Physical Port Mapping.
To rack mount the ZS-ZPA-APPL-800 appliance:
Align one rack mounting bracket to the screw holes on the side panel of the appliance, and secure the bracket using three A screws.
Secure the other rack mounting bracket to the other side of the appliance.
Ensure that the adapter's cable is connected and secured.

Hold the appliance and lift carefully to insert the appliance into the rack. Zscaler recommends installing a shelf in the rack to support the appliance. Attach the brackets to the rail rack using rack mounting screws.
Connect the necessary cables to the designated ports of the appliance. To learn more, see ZPA Appliance Physical Port Mapping.

The ZS-ZPA-APPL-8010-APPC / ZS-ZPA-APPL-8010-PSE appliances are 1U, 19-inch rack-mountable form factors. These instructions are structured to assist IT personnel with the physical mounting, cabling, and initial power on of the appliance. This guide solely focuses on the hardware installation process and doesn't cover software configuration. For software configuration, see Deploying App Connector and Private Service Edge ZPA Appliances.
The ZPA appliance has a weight of 18.96 lbs (8.6 kg), and its total packaged weight is 33 lbs (15 kg).

blocks.item: Before beginning the installation, verify that all necessary components are present in the packaging. The package includes the following items:
6x A screws for attaching the brackets to the appliance
6x B screws for mounting the appliance to the rack
Align one of the ear brackets to screw holes on the side of the chassis, and secure the brackets using 3x A screws.
Secure the other ear bracket to the other side of the appliance.
Insert the appliance into the rack with the ear brackets fixed on the posts using the B screws.
The method and parts required for mounting depend on whether a shelf or rail kit is used.
Connect the AC power cords to the appliance power supply unit. The appliance supports redundant power supply units (PSUs). Connect both cords to their respective power sources.

A continuous beep indicates that the second power source is unplugged or faulty. To silence the beep, press the round button located near or between the power supplies, or connect the second power source.

Connect the WAN cable to the designated port of the appliance. The appliance has several ports, including 10x 1GbE RJ45 ports and 8x 10G SFP+ ports. To learn more, see ZPA Appliance Physical Port Mapping.
You can deploy two or more appliances in a network location and pair them into groups for load balancing.

blocks.text: This section helps to identify and resolve common installation issues.

blocks.item: If the ZPA appliance does not boot:
Verify that the power outlet is active and functioning. A power LED light should be on. If not, it indicates a lack of power to the unit.
Check that the power supply is securely plugged into the unit and the power source.
Verify that the power LED light is on.

A continuous beeping sound indicates that only one power supply is active or that the power supply is defective. To stop the beeping, press the round button located near or between the power supplies. If the power supply is faulty, contact Zscaler Support to request a Return Merchandise Authorization (RMA).
If a network cable is connected, but no link light appears, there could be an issue with the cable, the port on the ZPA appliance, or the port on the connected switch.
Replace the cable with a new one to see if that resolves the issue.
If the problem persists, try connecting to a different port on the ZPA appliance to determine if the port is faulty.
Power cycle the device and confirm if the LED returns to a normal state.
